item.title: US, Ukraine meet in Geneva after Russia's massive overnight aerial barrage
item.description:
Ukraine's lead negotiator Rustem Umerov was set to meet US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Geneva on Thursday for bilateral talks focused on Ukraine's postwar economic recovery and preparations for a new round of trilateral negotiations with Russia expected in early March. The meeting came just hours after Russia launched one of its largest aerial assaults in months, firing 420 drones and 39 missiles at targets across eight Ukrainian regions overnight.

The Geneva session marks the latest effort by the Trump administration to maintain diplomatic momentum as the war enters its fifth year, with both sides still deadlocked over the fate of Russian-occupied Ukrainian territory.

item.title: NASA-backed study turns recycled sewage into lunar and Martian crop fertilizer
item.description:
Researchers working with NASA have demonstrated that recycled human and plant waste can be combined with simulated lunar and Martian soil to release nutrients essential for growing crops, a step toward making off-world agriculture sustainable for future space colonies.

The study, published in ACS Earth and Space Chemistry and highlighted in a press release this week by the American Chemical Society, describes how a nutrient-dense solution derived from processed sewage was mixed with materials designed to mimic the rocky, barren surfaces of the moon and Mars. The interaction released plant-essential elements including sulfur, calcium, and magnesium, offering early evidence that waste recycling could transform lifeless extraterrestrial terrain into something approaching farmable soil.

item.title: Google rolls out Nano Banana 2 as default AI image model across Gemini
item.description:
Google on Thursday unveiled Nano Banana 2, the latest version of its viral AI image generation tool, rolling it out as the default image model across the Gemini app, Google Search, and its video editing tool Flow. Officially designated Gemini 3.1 Flash Image, the upgrade brings capabilities previously reserved for the higher-end Nano Banana Pro model to a broader audience at faster speeds.

The new model produces images with resolutions ranging from 512 pixels to 4K across multiple aspect ratios, supports character consistency for up to five characters, and can maintain fidelity of up to 14 objects in a single workflow, according to TechCrunch. It also inherits Nano Banana Pro's advanced world knowledge, accurate text rendering, and the ability to generate data visualizations and infographics — features that made the Pro version popular among creators and professionals.

item.title: US demands Iran dismantle nuclear sites in tense Geneva talks
item.description: The United States and Iran on Thursday began a marathon third round of indirect nuclear negotiations in Geneva, with American envoys presenting sweeping demands for the dismantlement of Iran's main nuclear facilities as both sides race to avert a military confrontation.

item.title: US, Iran show 'unprecedented openness' in Geneva nuclear talks
item.description:
Iran and the United States held a third round of indirect nuclear negotiations in Geneva on Thursday, with Oman mediating the high-stakes talks as President Donald Trump's deadline for a deal rapidly approaches. The discussions, which adjourned for a midday break before resuming, were described by Iranian officials as having progressed "very intensely and very seriously," according to Bloomberg.

Oman's Foreign Minister Sayyid Badr Albusaidi, who has been shuttling between the two delegations at his country's embassy in Geneva, said the Iranian and American teams showed "unprecedented openness to new and creative ideas and solutions". The U.S. delegation is led by Trump's special Middle East envoy Steve Witkoff and his son-in-law Jared Kushner, while Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi heads Tehran's team.

item.title: Pentagon's kamikaze drone unit ready for Iran strikes
item.description:
The Pentagon's first one-way attack drone unit, Task Force Scorpion Strike, is operationally prepared to participate in potential strikes against Iran if President Donald Trump orders military action, according to Bloomberg, citing U.S. officials and analysts. The unit's readiness adds a new capability to an already massive American military buildup in the Middle East, where two aircraft carrier strike groups, stealth fighters, and long-range bombers are now positioned within striking range of Iran.

The development comes as the United States and Iran held a third round of indirect nuclear negotiations in Geneva on Thursday, with the two sides exchanging proposals through Omani mediators amid deepening uncertainty over whether diplomacy can avert a military confrontation.

item.title: Afghanistan launches border offensive against Pakistan
item.description: Afghanistan's Taliban forces launched what they described as large-scale offensive operations against Pakistani military positions along the Durand Line late Thursday, retaliating for Pakistani airstrikes earlier in the week that Kabul says killed civilians. Pakistan said it responded to what it called "unprovoked fire" across multiple sectors in its northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, with both sides claiming to have inflicted heavy casualties on the other. The exchange threatens to unravel a fragile ceasefire that had been in place since October 2025.

item.title: US, Iran to hold Vienna nuclear talks next week
item.description:
The United States and Iran will hold technical-level nuclear discussions next week in Vienna after concluding a third round of indirect negotiations in Geneva on Thursday, Oman's foreign minister announced.

"We have finished the day after significant progress in the negotiation between the United States and Iran," Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi wrote on X. "We will resume soon after consultation in the respective capitals. Discussions on a technical level will take place next week in Vienna."

The choice of Vienna, home to the International Atomic Energy Agency, underscores the increasingly technical nature of the negotiations over Tehran's nuclear program. IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi was present during Thursday's session, according to Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei.

item.title: Zelenskiy says next Ukraine-Russia talks to move to Abu Dhabi in early March
item.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy announced on Thursday that the next round of U.S.-brokered trilateral peace negotiations between Ukraine and Russia will likely take place in Abu Dhabi in early March, according to Reuters. The announcement came during Zelenskiy's evening address, following a day of preparatory bilateral talks in Geneva between Ukrainian and American officials focused on post-war reconstruction.

The Geneva meeting — led by Ukraine's chief negotiator Rustem Umerov and U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff alongside presidential adviser Jared Kushner — centered on a proposed "prosperity package" designed to mobilize public and private investment for Ukraine's economic recovery. Kyiv aims to attract roughly $800 billion over the next decade to rebuild the country, according to Reuters, while the World Bank's latest assessment estimates reconstruction costs at approximately $588 billion.

item.title: Oil prices rebound as Iran rejects uranium deal term
item.description: Oil prices swung sharply on Thursday, initially tumbling before reversing course, as traders weighed a massive buildup in U.S. crude inventories against signs that nuclear talks between Washington and Tehran were hitting a wall. The volatile session underscored the competing forces gripping global energy markets: ample domestic supply on one side, and the threat of military conflict in the Middle East on the other.

item.title: Scientists warn mega-constellations could devastate ozone layer
item.description: The race to fill low Earth orbit with vast fleets of satellites is raising alarms among atmospheric scientists, who warn that the mass burning of defunct spacecraft could damage the ozone layer and alter Earth's climate in ways that remain poorly understood. With SpaceX seeking permission to launch up to one million satellites and more than 1.23 million spacecraft now proposed worldwide, researchers and policymakers are calling for global regulation before the atmospheric consequences become irreversible.

item.title: UN denounces Taliban decree expanding executions and curbing rights
item.description: United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk on Thursday denounced a sweeping new Taliban decree that expands the use of the death penalty and permits corporal punishment for a range of offenses, including within the home, calling it a deepening of repression against the Afghan people and particularly women and girls.

item.title: Russia says it downed 220 Ukrainian drones over nine hours
item.description: Russia's Defence Ministry said on Thursday that its air defense systems intercepted 220 Ukrainian drones over a nine-hour period, including 24 headed for Moscow, in one of the largest reported waves of Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian territory this year. The interceptions came on the same day that Russia launched a mass overnight strike on Ukraine involving 420 drones and 39 missiles, and as U.S. and Ukrainian envoys met in Geneva to discuss paths to ending the war.

item.title: 171 bodies found in mass graves near Congo's Uvira after M23 withdrawal
item.description: Congolese authorities on Thursday announced the discovery of two mass graves containing at least 171 bodies on the outskirts of the eastern city of Uvira, in an area the M23 rebel group recently vacated. The grim find underscores the toll of escalating violence in the region, which has persisted despite a U.S.-brokered peace deal between the Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda.

item.title: Syria, Druze factions complete first prisoner swap since summer clashes
item.description: The Syrian government and Druze factions controlling the southern city of Sweida carried out their first prisoner exchange on Thursday since deadly sectarian clashes erupted last summer, according to the Syrian government's Sweida media office. The swap marks a rare step toward a political resolution in one of the last regions of the country still outside Damascus's control.

item.title: Maduro asks judge to toss drug indictment over blocked legal fees
item.description:
Lawyers for ousted Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro filed a motion on Thursday in Manhattan federal court asking a judge to dismiss the indictment against him, arguing that the U.S. government has unconstitutionally blocked Venezuelan funds from paying his legal costs in violation of his Sixth Amendment right to counsel.

Attorney Barry Pollack submitted the filing in the Southern District of New York, asserting that the Trump administration's refusal to allow the Venezuelan government to cover Maduro's defense amounts to a due process violation that would render any trial "constitutionally defective," according to the Associated Press.

item.title: US and Congo sign $1.2B health deal amid African data-sharing concerns
item.description:
The United States and the Democratic Republic of Congo on Thursday signed a $1.2 billion health partnership, making the DRC the 19th country to enter a bilateral health agreement under the Trump administration's "America First Global Health Strategy."

The five-year memorandum of understanding, spanning 2026 to 2031, includes up to $900 million in U.S. government assistance and a commitment from the Congolese government to increase its domestic health spending by $300 million over the same period, according to a joint statement from the two governments.

item.title: Venezuela suspends 19 Maduro-era oil contracts
item.description:
Venezuela's oil ministry has suspended 19 oil production-sharing contracts with private companies that were signed under the administration of former President Nicolás Maduro, according to four sources with knowledge of the move who spoke to Reuters.

The suspension has had no impact on the country's oil and gas output so far, the sources said. State oil company PDVSA continues to sell crude produced under the contracts while they are under review. Both the Venezuelan and U.S. governments are now scrutinizing the credentials of the firms involved and may recommend revoking some of the agreements.

item.title: Germany votes to let military intercept drones
item.description:
Germany's parliament on Thursday voted to expand the military's authority to intercept or shoot down drones, responding to a surge in unidentified aerial activity that officials have linked to Russia's hybrid warfare campaign against Europe.

The Bundestag approved an amendment to the country's air security law with support from the governing conservatives, the Social Democrats, and the far-right Alternative for Germany opposition, according to Reuters. The legislation marks the culmination of months of political urgency over rogue drones spotted near airports, military bases, and critical infrastructure across the country.

item.title: Pakistan declares 'open war' on Afghanistan after deadly border clashes
item.description:
Pakistan and Afghanistan plunged into their most dangerous military confrontation in years as the Taliban launched a large-scale ground offensive against Pakistani positions along the disputed Durand Line on Thursday evening, prompting Pakistani airstrikes on Kabul, Kandahar, and Paktia province hours later. Pakistan's Defence Minister Khawaja Asif declared "open war" against Afghanistan on Friday, posting on X: "Our patience has reached its limit. Now it is open war between us and you."

The rapidly escalating conflict, unfolding during the Muslim holy month of Ramadan, has shattered a fragile ceasefire brokered by Qatar last October and drawn the nuclear-armed neighbors into their most direct military engagement since the Taliban seized power in 2021.
